//: The four shipping projects, named one by one rather than globbed as ../src/**/*.csproj. A glob would
silently pick up a fifth project the day one is added -- .FlatFiles is already planned (#22) -- and
whether it belongs in the published reference is a decision somebody should make in a diff. DocsSiteTests
pins this list to the projects under src/, so the decision cannot be skipped by omission in either
direction, the same bargain PublishWorkflowTests makes for the PACKAGES list.
TargetFramework is pinned because DocFX loads these through MSBuildWorkspace and a multi-targeted project
would otherwise be ambiguous. D7 says net10.0 only; the property keeps this honest if that ever changes.
Content is enumerated rather than globbed as **/*.md for one concrete reason: docs/superpowers/ holds the
designs, plans and measurements, which are working material. A broad glob would publish the next plan
somebody writes. What is listed is what is meant for a reader.
README.md and CHANGELOG.md are the repository's own files, rendered from the same source: one copy of each,
on GitHub, inside all four packages, and here. DocFX accepts the relative parent path (and rejects an
absolute one). A file pulled from .. lands at the site root, which is why README's own links to repository
files -- LICENSE, and the allocation figures -- are absolute URLs rather than relative paths: a relative
one cannot resolve from both the repository root and the site root, and it is already meaningless inside
the four packages this README is packed into. docs/performance/ is published on its own, at the path the
landing page links to. It cannot ride in the .. entry: DocFX aborts outright on a nested path there,
"Relative to path has too many '../'".
docs/reconciliation/ is left out for the same reason superpowers/ is -- a spec-versus-docs-site diff and
the script that produced it are working material, not a page anybody should land on.
//sitemap: The one place in this repository that spells out the public URL. DocFX emits relative links everywhere
else, which is why the site works unchanged under a /massivedotnet/ path -- but a sitemap has to carry
absolute ones. If this ever needs to change, the reason will be a Pages setting outside this repository.

globalMetadata._appFooter: MassiveDotNet -- an independent .NET 10 SDK for the Massive market data platform. MIT. The README is the reference; where this site and the README disagree, the README wins.
